name: travel-agent: final response hard v2
description: Whole-trip requests a plausible planner gets wrong, so the score can move; `travel-agent: final response` is the regression set expected to stay at 1. Run with --repetitions for a pass rate. Graded by rubric, plus code checks read from every search the run made, the subagents' included: `expected_calls` and `forbidden_arguments` take the availability-scout shape, and `budget_given: false` fails any summarize_budget call that supplies a budget the traveler never gave. Assumes TRAVEL_AGENT_PROVIDER=sample-data. `no-budget` cannot pass its code check until summarize_budget accepts a plan with no budget; it is here to measure that change. v2 rewrites two criteria in nights-contradict-dates that failed correct runs: a conditional "labels any prices" failed every run that rightly asked before quoting any, because the judge reads silent evidence as not met, so conditional criteria are now phrased as prohibitions; and "one concise question" failed a run whose extra questions were marked optional, which the prompt does not forbid.

messages.content: Plan 5 nights in Kyoto for 2 people flying from SFO, 2027-04-05 to 2027-04-08. Budget $4000.

criteria: Notices that 2027-04-05 to 2027-04-08 is 3 nights, not 5.
Either asks which is right, or states the reading it chose and plans on it throughout.
Does not make the traveler answer anything routine before it proceeds, such as cabin class, which defaults to economy; extra questions are fine only when marked optional.
Does not present a plan whose nights, lodging and dates disagree with each other.
Does not quote any flight or lodging price without labelling it as sample data.

metadata.trap: Two readings give materially different trips, which is exactly when the prompt says to check in; silently picking one is the failure.

messages.content: Plan 4 days in Lisbon for 2 people flying from Boston, 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-14. We haven't set a budget yet; tell us what it would cost.

criteria: States an estimated total for the trip.
Does not describe the plan as within or over a budget, since none was given.
Labels flight and lodging prices as sample data.

metadata.trap: A real run with no budget passed summarize_budget an invented $1500 as a 'reference line'. The tool requires a budget, so it cannot be called honestly here.
metadata.known_gap: summarize_budget rejects a call with no budget_total, so budget_not_invented fails until the tool accepts one.

messages.content: 4 of us are meeting in Lisbon, 2027-06-07 to 2027-06-12: two flying from San Francisco (SFO) and two from New York (JFK). Find flights and one place for all four to stay. Budget $9000 total.

criteria: Prices flights separately for the two travelers from SFO and the two from JFK.
Finds lodging for all four together.
States the total for the group against the $9000 budget.
Labels flight and lodging prices as sample data.

metadata.trap: The group has one destination and one budget, so one search for 4 travelers from a single airport reads naturally and prices half the group from the wrong city.
